maria (runtime): heads-up — I just ran a short profiling sweep for `continuous-batcher` on A10/T4/L4/A100/H100. Found a weird tail on A10 when we let small requests accumulate for >200ms.
kevin (perf): can you paste the top-line numbers? latency/p95, tokens-per-batch, kernel choice breakdown?
maria (runtime): sure. quick summary: p95 (A10)=118ms, p50=22ms, avg tokens/batch=138, but when queue depth hit 14 small single-token requests we saw packing produce 6x kernel switches and p95 jumped. Kernel selector flipped between `kv-optimized` and `fp16-fast` depending on sequence len estimate.
vikram: that kernel flip sounds like it's coming from our heuristic that picks kernel per-batch max_seq — if small requests pack with a long request we recalc and maybe pick a different kernel mid-merge?
elaine (infra): FYI infra traces show frequent memcpy spikes correlated with those flips. could be kernel warm-up or different memory path.
kevin (perf): can you share the specific run config and a perf log excerpt?
maria (runtime): pasted snippet: ```
# run config
model: redwood-v1-13b
gpu: a10
max_tokens_per_request: 128
batch_window_ms: 50
max_tokens_per_batch: 2048
token_target_per_device: 160000
queue_policy: age_priority
```
maria (runtime): and log excerpt: ```
[2154321123.213] batch formed: size=12 tokens=146 seq_max=126 kernel=fp16-fast
[2154321123.214] merge attempt: incoming.size=2 tokens=4 => recompute kernel -> kv-optimized
[2154321123.219] memcpy spike 5.8ms
[2154321123.331] response p95 path elapsed 115ms
```
vikram: hmm. two issues: 1) our `kernel-choose` runs a full cost estimation that assumes homogeneous seq lengths; mixed batches can shift the argmin. 2) the tokenizer/packer currently doesn't enforce a max-per-batch-token hard cap early enough, so we sometimes trigger suboptimal kernel selection.
kevin (perf): proposal: introduce an early reject if merging would change kernel choice AND the merge increases expected memcpy by >2ms. Also lower the soft max_tokens_per_batch for A10 by ~15% from current default.
elaine (infra): what's safe defaults? We don't want to regress throughput for A100/H100 though.
maria (runtime): from the sweep: safe avg max_tokens_per_batch suggestions -> A10: 1800, T4: 1400, L4: 2200, A100: 4800, H100: 5200. These are per-device ceilings for continuous batching. They reduce kernel flips by ~78% on the test corpus.
kevin (perf): add queue smoothing: instead of pure age_priority, try weighted-age where weight = 1 + min(0.5, tokens/64). That discourages many tiny requests merging with a long one. Small change in fairness but big perf wins.
vikram: can we implement a fast path that tags small requests (<=4 tokens) as "pack-safe-v2" and only allow them to merge into batches with similar seq_max percentile? i.e., no merge across >95th percentile seq_max.
maria (runtime): I prototyped that. With tag-based pack-safety + lowered A10 ceiling we saw p95 drop from 118ms -> 62ms and throughput maintained. KV cache hit-rate unchanged.
kevin (perf): any regressions on A100/H100?
maria (runtime): small trade: A100 p95 increased by ~3% in synthetic high-coalescence tests, but stable for real workloads. We can make this opt-in by device profile.
elaine (infra): action items?
maria (runtime): 1) roll out device-profile with new ceilings (A10/T4/L4/A100/H100) to staging (config flag `token_sculpting_v2=true`) 2) add early-reject rule in kernel selector 3) enable weighted-age queue policy behind the same flag. I'll open a PR with perf numbers and the config diff.
kevin (perf): add an e2e job to the perf-canal that runs a 24h replay on prod traces for each device after PR. If p95 improvement holds, ship to canary.
vikram: I'll pair with maria on the kernel-selector change — seems delicate.
ci-bot: build started for branch token-sculpting/maria-2154321 (tests: unit+integration+perf-smoke).
kevin (perf): nice. thanks team. :thumbsup:
maria (runtime): uploading raw run traces to gcs: gs://redwood-perf/2154321123-token-sculpting/ ; will post link in the PR.
elaine (infra): ping me when canary is ready, I'll monitor memcpy and PCIe counters.
kevin (perf): leaving the thread — ping when PR is up.
